motivation: Follow-up after single-code external intervention produced only six adaptive/fixed discordances in1500 puzzles; previous endpoint retained, not replaced.

calibration.selection: first16 archived batches in original training extraction; no new or old held-out outcomes
calibration.replacements: uniform other code, nested seeded positions and values per puzzle
calibration.dose_selection: smallest count causing >=0.10 absolute decrease in fixed-tail verified resolution relative to clean, on training only; if none, stop without new stress corpus

external.exclude: official solutions, generator pilot32, old correction external1000 and native-dynamics external2000, plus within-corpus digit and dihedral transformations

primary: adaptive verified resolution rate minus fixed-clean-tail verified resolution rate after the selected level8 corruption
intervention: one fixed number of level8 codes replaced with random alternatives from the same codebook, same positions/replacements for adaptive and fixed-tail; subsequent levels9..12 adaptive versus original clean codes
controls: sham forces original selected codes and must be bitwise equal
codes1..7 unchanged, exactly selected level8 codes altered
no native forward or decoded gold solution given to generator
secondary: gain in initially blank cell accuracy
latent directional compensation and final-distance ratio
fixed-tail error induction and adaptive recovery among clean solved puzzles
interval: 10000 paired puzzle bootstrap,99 percent two-sided for primary,seed20261212; exact paired sign/McNemar test also reported
power: fixed n1000, sensitivity calculated from training fixed-tail damage before new outputs, no universal power or training-variance guarantee
status: new locally specified exploratory follow-up after prior results, own reserved corpus, not a single confirmatory family with previous studies
limits: strong artificial corruption may be out of distribution
training code corruption described in source paper; no checkpoint without corruption to identify its effect
first-order robustness and error correction not sufficient for second-order reliability monitoring
subset conditioned on clean success only secondary
